title: Speaking & Writing
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata tambahan dan memahami teks tentang memberikan informasi pribadi.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 14-15
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to ask and answer questions about themselves.
Learners will be able to make a good impression when they meet people.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feeling. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes down his/her name on the board (e.g. Susan)
Ask the student if their name starts with the shown letter (e.g. starts with S) and then they must stand up and introduce themselves. Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 18.
First, the teacher reads the questions in the speech bubble at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear.
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the questions aloud as a class.
Then, ask students to ask and answer the questions, in pairs.
Model to the students how the questions can be changed by changing some of the key vocabulary in the questions.

Now, put them in different pairs and ask them to substitute some of the key vocabulary in the questions so they can practice asking about different things. This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs.
To finish the speaking activity, elicit responses from some students by asking the questions in the speech bubbles with the original vocabulary, and also with some substituted vocabulary.
Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes). This can be used to help answer students' questions.

Ask students to look at Student Book page 14 and read the instructions, and ask some instruction-checking questions to check if students understand the task, e.g. Which activity are we doing? What page is it on? What do you have to do?
Read the questions aloud together as a class.
Put students in pairs and tell them to practice asking and answering the questions with their partner. The answers must be written in complete sentences.
Remind students to follow the structures shown in the Q&A models and Language Box examples on this page.
Give students around 8-10 minutes to complete the task.
Elicit answers from the class. Answers will vary due to students’ own personal information.
Put students in new pairs and ask them to practice asking and answering the questions again.
Ask some students to share their answers about their partner with the class.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Students will play a game. The teacher will say an answer, and the students have to ask the questions. (This is like the game ‘Jeopardy’).
Below is an example of how to start the game.
The teacher says, "The answer is ‘My name is (Miss Mary)’ and then asks, “What is the question?” Students should answer, “What is your name?”
Other examples:
"The answer is ‘August 17th’." (use your own birthday here)
"The answer is - ‘I live far from the school’." (use your own information here)
"The answer is ‘I live with my family’." (use your own information here)
Then put students into groups of three or four. Tell them to take turns saying answers and the other members of the group should say the questions.
Tell students to make sure each student in the group says at least two answers each.
To end the activity, elicit some examples from some students.
Direct the students to look at the pictures on page 15 and ask them ‘“What can you see on the page?” to elicit some answers.
Next, tell students to read the text about the Teen Value. They can read it silently, or put them in pairs to share reading the text aloud together, sentence by sentence.
Elicit from students, “What is the key focus of this Teen Corner page?”, and “Why do you think this skill (or value) is important?”
Ask students to look at activity A and give them around 3-4 minutes to discuss how the students in the picture are making a good impression.
Ask students to look at activity B and then say the words under pictures 1-8 and let the students after you.
Ask them to discuss the pictures and tick the ones that can make a good impression, and cross the ones that would not.
Give them around 3-4 minutes to complete the task.
Instead of simply saying “yes” or “no,” the activity can be made more engaging by involving movements. Students step to the left if the answer is ✓ and they step to the right if the answer is ✗.
Next, prepare students for the speaking activity. They have to introduce themselves to their group and make a good impression.

Give students about 5 minutes to brainstorm and write down information that they can talk about when they introduce themselves as mentioned in the blue boxes; age and birthday, where they live, who they live with, things they like and don’t like.
Put students into new groups of three or four students. • Tell students that each student must introduce themselves, and that they have 2 minutes each to speak.

Move around the classroom to make sure that all students are taking part in the conversations, are introducing themselves, and are using the skills shared in the ‘Making a good impression’ box on this page
Below are sample answers that can be shown to students and model them before they do their task if they need lots of support.

“Hello! My name is Alex. I am thirteen years old. My birthday is on July 12. I live near the library. I live with my parents and my sister. I like basketball and music. I don’t like waking up early. Nice to meet you.”

“Hi! I’m Amy. I am twelve years old. My birthday is on March 5. I live on Green Street with my mum, dad, and my brother. I like drawing and watching movies. I don’t like spiders. It’s good to meet you.”
Ask students to look at activity D and read the two discussion questions aloud to the class.
Tell students that they have around 5 minutes to discuss the questions and write their own answers.
They don’t have to write the same answers as their group. Some possible answers:
Question 1: I feel a little shy / I feel confident when I talk to others
Question 2: I can smile and look at people / I can speak politely
Finish the class by reminding students that we should try to make a good impression of ourselves when we meet people, but also when we’re talking to friends and family.
Teachers can do a quick survey by referring to the responses from previous activity. For example: “Who feels shy when they introduce themselves? Who feels confident?”
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: unjuk kerja speaking berpasangan (kelancaran, ketepatan, keberanian).
Produk tulisan sederhana sesuai model di Student Book (struktur & kosakata unit).
Umpan balik teman sebaya dan guru terhadap hasil speaking/writing.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
